newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: James Hardie eyes Japanese housing market.
newsitem.headline: James Hardie eyes Japanese housing market.

text.p: Building products manufacturer James Hardie Industries Ltd said on Thursday it was looking at entering the Japanese housing market through Japanese house builder, Sekisui Chemical Co.

"We have trials going on now with Sekisumi Chemical. We are working with them to develop a cladding system to go over the top of the external walls of houses," James Hardie's managing director, Keith Barton, told reporters after the company's annual meeting.
Barton said the company would know in the next 12 months if the trials were successful or not.
"We really have to wait and see how this works. If it is successful, it (Japan) is a large market," he said.
The Japanese housing market, estimated to be worth about A$320 billion a year, is in the process of being deregulated to give greater access to foreign manufacturers.
If the trials were a success, James Hardie would export fibre cement product to Japan from Australia and possibly from its plant in the Phillipines which is still under construction, Barton said.
"Our major Asian export market at the moment is the Phillipines - The plant should be ready for commissioning in about 14 months time," he said.
Barton said apart from the Phillipines and Japan, James Hardie was in the process of building its fibre cement business in Indonesia, Singapore and Korea.
But the United States was still the key focus of the group's expansion plans, Barton said.
"It (the U.S. operations) has the highest growth and is the biggest profit earner and should continue to be that for at least the next five years," he said.
James Hardie shares closed one cent firmer at A$4.43.
